title: When activation is withheld
blurb: Tracks real launch deliveries across document reloads in sessionStorage and maps every exclusion in the spec and Chromium's LaunchQueue::SendLaunchParams() rule alongside runtime feature-detection migration code.
question: Which launch modes, navigation states, and reload re-deliveries intentionally withhold user activation, and how should apps feature-detect the grant safely across Chrome versions?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 (tab mode), reloading produced previous=navigate/0 deliveries and this=reload/0 deliveries with no re-delivery, and the path explorer flipped granted vs not granted across focus-existing, navigate-new, and kill-switch-off states. Installed-app reload verification not run in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (tab reload and path model verified); installed-app reload not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Activation is withheld for navigating launches, out-of-scope windows, non-user launches, reload re-delivery, and when the kill switch is disabled
friction.repro: Check navigator.userActivation.isActive inside launchQueue.setConsumer() on an initial app launch, navigate-new/navigate-existing launch, or with --disable-features=WebAppLaunchHandlerUserActivation; it is false even on Chrome 160+.
friction.workaround: Feature-detect navigator.userActivation?.isActive at runtime inside every consumer invocation and keep an in-app click fallback instead of branching on Chrome version.
